correctness.rationale: The source dimensions and facet descriptions are explicit. Independent permutations of the three indices act orthogonally and transitively on coordinates, so the orthogonal projector onto either affine translation space has constant diagonal. Its trace is the source dimension, proving that every squared projected coordinate-normal length equals dimension divided by \(n^3\). Dividing the uniform coordinate slack by this norm gives the displayed radii. Summing the coordinate-clearance inequalities gives matching global upper bounds, and equality forces every coordinate of an optimal center to equal the uniform value, proving uniqueness.

value.rationale: These stochastic tensor polytopes are natural higher-dimensional Birkhoff-type objects whose vertex enumeration remains difficult and is the main subject of the source. The result gives a complete intrinsic inball theorem for both canonical order-3 stochasticity notions without requiring their vertices: exact radius, unique center, and tangency of every facet. The dimension-controlled normal identity also explains why two very different constraint systems nevertheless have closed all-dimensional metric formulas.
